title: sdks: unify auth/retries, improve streaming ergonomics, parity fixes, bump versions to v1.201.0
author: Ethan Kim
description: Overview: This PR unifies auth and retry behaviors across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, improves streaming ergonomics (client-side backpressure + reconnect), applies parity fixes across language bindings, and bumps SDK versions to v1.201.0. Motivation: Customers reported inconsistent auth header handling and different retry semantics across SDKs which led to user confusion and operational incidents (see ENG-2345). Streaming ergonomics and error handling differences made cross-language example parity difficult and increased support load. Goals: (1) Standardize auth token refresh and header propagation, (2) Provide a common retry policy implementation (idempotency-aware + configurable backoff), (3) Improve streaming API ergonomics (simple reconnect, clearer progress events, safer cancellation), (4) Align public surface and examples across Python/TS/Go, (5) Ship version bump to v1.201.0 with release notes. What changed (high level): - Introduced a common auth adapter interface (language-specific implementations) that centralizes token refresh and header enrichment. - Replaced ad-hoc retry loops with a shared retry-policy util that supports idempotency markers, pluggable backoff strategies, and a global per-SDK default. - Streaming: added client reconnect helper, standardized progress/cancel events, and improved backpressure handling in the TypeScript and Go streaming clients; Python streaming received a compatibility shim to keep existing sync/async ergonomics. - Parity fixes: normalized error types/messages, updated examples and tests for chat streaming and function-calling across SDKs. - Docs/examples updated and added migration notes. Commits (summary): - unify: add auth adapter and common retry-policy (python/ts/go) - streaming: add reconnect/backpressure helpers and upgrade examples - parity: align error codes and messages across SDKs - docs: update quickstarts, migration guide, changelog - release: bump versions to v1.201.0 and update package metadata Files touched (high-level): - sdk/python/redwood/auth.py - sdk/python/redwood/retries.py - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py - sdk/typescript/src/auth.ts - sdk/typescript/src/retries.ts - sdk/typescript/src/streaming.ts - sdk/go/auth/auth.go - sdk/go/retries/retries.go - sdk/go/streaming/streaming.go - docs/quickstarts/sdk-migration.md - examples/multi-lang/streaming/* Tests: Added unit tests for retry backoff and idempotency, e2e tests for streaming reconnects (flaky on first run, flake fixed in subsequent commit). CI: github/workflows/ci.yaml runs per-language test matrices; initial run showed a flaky TS streaming test which was addressed by adding deterministic timing in the reconnect test. Backwards compatibility: The Python SDK exposes a compatibility shim so breaking changes are minimal; migration notes included for advanced users who override retry/auth behaviors. Checklist: - [x] Add common auth adapter and implement in Python/TS/Go - [x] Replace retry loops with shared policy and tests - [x] Improve streaming ergonomics and add e2e tests - [x] Update examples and docs - [x] Bump versions and changelog - [x] Get approvals and run full CI Review notes: See review_comments for detailed threads. Related: Linear ENG-2345, PM-678 for release coordination, and an internal docs task ENG-2401. Merge: Squash-and-merge to main with release commit and changelog entry.

streaming: add reconnect and backpressure helpers (ts/go) and shims for python
